gmp.reason: gmp.sh downloads a GNU tarball (GMP_VER=6.3.0) via dep_version, not git; no canonical git mirror with a matching v6.3.0 tag was found (checked github.com/alisw/GMP and git.savannah.gnu.org/git/gmp — neither has it), so origin/tag here describe the tarball, not a clonable git ref; tag is the bare tarball-filename version. 6.3. Tracked via the tarball-listing custom datasource against releasesUrl, so a new upstream release still raises a PR.

nv-codec.reason: Pinned to the SDK 13.0 line for driver compatibility. Each nv-codec-headers SDK line sets a minimum NVIDIA driver, and FFmpeg's NVENC refuses to open on anything older ('Driver does not support the required nvenc API version'): sdk/13.0 needs 570+, sdk/13.1 needs 610+. NVIDIA's 580 branch is the LAST driver for Maxwell/Pascal/Volta (GTX 900/10-series), so 13.1 headers would break NVENC on those cards permanently, and on any machine not yet on 610 (measured: RTX 3080 on Windows driver 591.86). Both FFmpeg lines accept ffnvcodec >= 12.1.14.0, and the 13.1-only features (newer counting fields, AV1 hierarchical refs) sit behind version guards with fallbacks, so 13.0 loses optional features, not builds. See hold.

hold.liftWhen: Review, never lift automatically, when: an FFmpeg line we ship requires ffnvcodec >= 13.1 (consider a per-line override rather than raising every line's floor); NVIDIA ends the 580 branch (lifting still retires NVENC on Maxwell/Pascal/Volta -- that is a policy decision, not a consequence); or a 13.1+ NVENC feature is worth raising the driver floor to 610. Re-run a real NVENC encode on the oldest driver the new floor claims.

vulkan-shim.reason: No release tags; pinned reviewed master HEAD. Static stub that LoadLibrary/dlopens the real Vulkan loader at runtime so Windows artifacts carry no hard vulkan-1.dll import - BtbN/FFmpeg-Builds uses the same shim for the same reason.

libgsm.reason: libgsm.sh downloads https://www.quut.com/gsm/gsm-<tag>.tar.gz via dep_version, not git; there is no clean canonical upstream git repo (the code ships as a hand-packed tarball with a non-standard Makefile). origin is the release DIRECTORY, deliberately without a version in it: Renovate's tarball manager updates `tag` only, so a versioned origin URL goes stale on the first bump -- which is exactly what happened here (origin said 1.0.22 while tag was 1.0.24). tag is the bare tarball-filename version. Tracked via the tarball-listing custom datasource against releasesUrl, so a new upstream release still raises a PR.

mbedtls.reason: Renovate tracks the git tag (git-tags on origin), but mbedtls.sh downloads the matching release tarball (mbedtls-<ver>.tar.bz2, v stripped) instead of cloning — the tarball bundles the 'framework' submodule in-tree, avoiding a submodule init. Pin the 3.6 LTS line (4.x is the TF-PSA-Crypto split, not yet consumed by FFmpeg/SRT/librist). Held at 3.x by a renovate.json allowedVersions rule (see hold): mbedTLS 4 removed ctr_drbg.h/entropy.h (moved to PSA Crypto). The consumers here are SRT and librist, not FFmpeg's TLS layer (OpenSSL/GnuTLS/SChannel), so the hold lifts on THEIR mbedTLS 4 support. Tracked in issue #18.

hold.liftWhen: Review when the SRT and librist versions we ship build and link against mbedTLS 4 (its TF-PSA-Crypto split) through this repo's mbedtls.sh recipe -- those transports, not FFmpeg's TLS layer (OpenSSL/GnuTLS/SChannel here), are what consume it. Verify encrypted SRT and RIST transport before lifting.
